message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_a92250a89e31", "mechanism": "The first m_axis_tdata output occurs when the state machine transitions from STATE_IDLE to STATE_OUTPUT_DATA on trigger. The original code sets store_output=1'b1 unconditionally, but m_axis_tdata_int is only driven when m_axis_tready_int_reg is already asserted. If the downstream m_axis_tready is not ready at that exact cycle, the first payload byte is never emitted, causing m_axis_tdata to stay zero at the first mismatch cycle. Replacing the unconditional store_output with m_axis_tvalid (the downstream ready/valid handshake) aligns the capture of counters with the cycle when the output channel can actually accept data, so the first byte appears on the expected cycle."}, {"id": "patch_f2d9d35bb697", "mechanism": "In the IDLE state, the transition to STATE_OUTPUT_DATA and the first output byte are gated only by trigger. The simulation shows m_axis_tdata stuck at zero on the first few trigger events, implying the output channel was not ready. Adding m_axis_tready_int_reg to the condition ensures the state only advances when the internal ready flag indicates the output pipeline can accept a new frame, preventing premature state transitions that produce zero payloads."}, {"id": "patch_7329800dc4a8", "mechanism": "busy_reg is assigned 1'b0 in the sequential block but the oracle expects it to reflect monitor_axis_tready activity. The first mismatches coincide with cycles where monitor_axis_tready toggles, suggesting busy should follow the monitor-side ready rather than being hard-wired low. Using monitor_axis_tready as the RHS makes busy pulse with the monitor interface, matching the observed trace."}, {"id": "patch_0b3ab7ce9c6c", "mechanism": "frame_count_reg is reset to 0 every cycle in the sequential block, yet the test expects frame counts to accumulate. The first mismatches appear when a new frame starts; if frame_count_reg stays zero, the byte emitted for the frame-count field is zero instead of the incremented value. Substituting byte_count_next (which increments on monitor_axis_tvalid & monitor_axis_tready) provides a monotonically increasing value that matches the expected frame-count byte pattern."}, {"id": "patch_c98c57628a2e", "mechanism": "store_output is hard-wired to 1'b1 in the IDLE->OUTPUT transition, capturing counters before the output channel is ready. The oracle expects the capture to happen when m_axis_tvalid is asserted, meaning the downstream has accepted the previous frame. Replacing the constant with m_axis_tvalid defers the snapshot until the output side signals readiness, aligning the first output byte with the expected cycle."}, {"id": "patch_f5b5b7b84f2e", "mechanism": "temp_m_axis_tlast_reg is initialized to 1'b0 but never driven by a related monitor signal. The first mismatches show m_axis_tdata=0 when the monitor side signals tlast, suggesting the internal last flag should track monitor_axis_tready (which coincides with tlast in the trace). Using monitor_axis_tready as the RHS propagates the monitor last indication into the output pipeline, allowing the correct frame-termination byte to appear."}, {"id": "patch_dcfe3aa1fa32", "mechanism": "busy_reg is set to 1'b0 in the reset block, but the trace expects busy to assert when the output pipeline accepts a new frame (store_axis_int_to_output). The first mismatches occur at cycles where this store signal pulses. Driving busy_reg with store_axis_int_to_output makes busy follow the actual frame-start event, matching the observed busy/m_axis_tdata correlation."}, {"id": "patch_a691a4237cc9", "mechanism": "busy_reg is initialized to 1'b0, yet the earliest mismatch shows m_axis_tdata should be non-zero, implying busy should already be asserted. m_axis_tuser_reg is a register that toggles with frame emission; using it as the reset value for busy_reg seeds busy with the correct frame-active state, so the first output byte appears instead of zero."}], "explanation": "All eight patches target the first observed mismatch at cycle 35 where m_axis_tdata is 0 but should be 1. The root cause cluster is the IDLE-to-OUTPUT transition: store_output fires unconditionally on trigger, but the output channel isn't ready, so the first payload byte is lost. Patches a92250a89e31, f2d9d35bb697, and c98c57628a2e directly gate this transition with downstream ready/valid signals. The remaining patches (7329800dc4a8, 0b3ab7ce9c6c, f5b5b7b84f2e, dcfe3aa1fa32, a691a4237cc9) adjust auxiliary registers (busy, frame_count, temp last flags) that correlate with the same handshake timing, providing secondary alignment. Together they cover the handshake gating, counter capture, and status propagation needed to make the first output byte appear on cycle 35."}
